claim: Let \(\alpha(a)=(a,247/250-a,3/500,3/500)\) and \(\beta=(19/20,3/100,1/50,0)\), with \(9/10\le a<19/20\). If deterministic LOCC self-catalysis with \(N\) catalyst copies is possible, i.e. \[\alpha(a)^{\otimes(N+1)}\prec\beta\otimes\alpha(a)^{\otimes N},\]then necessarily \[N\ge R(a):=\frac{40a}{(19-20a)(247-250a)}.\]The bound comes from the single majorization prefix of length \(N+2\), whose source sum is \(a^N[a+(N+1)(247/250-a)]\) and whose target sum is \(a^{N-1}[(49/50)a+(19/20)N(247/250-a)]\). Consequently every successful self-catalytic conversion in this family needs at least \(\lceil R(a)\rceil\) catalyst copies, and \[R(a)=\frac{1}{5(19/20-a)}-\frac{104}{19}+O(19/20-a)\]as \(a\uparrow19/20\). Thus no fixed finite catalyst-copy budget works uniformly along the family. For the five multi-copy examples tabulated by Duarte, Drumond, and Terra Cunha at \(a=0.900,0.908,0.918,0.925,0.928\), the lower bounds are respectively \(18/11,227/105,459/140,296/63,928/165\), whose ceilings are \(2,3,4,5,6\). Combined with the successful conversions recorded in their Table I, this gives a single analytic certificate of the minimal copy counts for all five rows.

correctness.rationale: The largest N+2 product entries have a fixed ordering on the stated interval. Their Nielsen-prefix inequality simplifies exactly to N(20a-19)(250a-247)>=40a. The denominator is positive, yielding the bound, and its endpoint asymptotic is explicit. Exact tensor-product replay confirms all five source-table minima.
